questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes CRM software actually useful to a business?
options: Having the most expensive CRM license available
The software combined with the discipline of actually using it, not the software alone
Only sales reps are allowed to see any of the data
Replacing every spreadsheet with a single printed binder
questions.explain: The lesson states that software without the discipline of using it is just an expensive, out-of-date address book — both halves matter.

questions.q: Which CRM platform does this lesson describe as having grown out of a marketing platform, known for an easier learning curve?
options: SAP
Microsoft Dynamics 365
Pipedrive
HubSpot
questions.explain: HubSpot started as a marketing platform and grew a full CRM around it, with strong adoption among small and mid-sized businesses.

questions.q: What does an 'account' record represent in a CRM?
options: A specific potential deal
The company (or household) a business sells to
A single unqualified lead
A support ticket
questions.explain: An account represents the organization being sold to — company-level information like industry, size, and billing address.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is CRM actually built to solve across the lifecycle?
options: Replacing marketing, sales, and service teams with a single employee
Making sure only one team ever touches a given customer
Eliminating the need for any handoffs between teams
Keeping one continuous, trustworthy record as a person moves from stranger to lead to opportunity to customer
questions.explain: Each stage isn't hard to imagine as a separate tool — what's hard is the continuity across the handoffs, which is exactly what a shared system provides.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real measure of CRM success?
options: The total number of software licenses purchased
Whether the numbers coming out of the system are trustworthy and actionable, not just that the software was adopted
How many employees log in at least once a month
How visually appealing the CRM's dashboards look
questions.explain: Buying licenses isn't the goal — the data inside has to be reliable enough that leadership can actually act on the numbers it produces.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish a developer's work from an administrator's?
options: A developer only fixes bugs reported by administrators
There is no real difference between the two roles
A developer exclusively manages user permissions and security settings
A developer builds custom logic, integrations, and new applications on the platform, while an admin customizes what's already there
questions.explain: Where an admin customizes existing, pre-built applications, a developer builds genuinely new things directly on the platform.

questions.q: Besides full applications, what else does this lesson say is listed on AppExchange?
options: Only free trial licenses for Salesforce itself
Only mobile phone hardware
Nothing else — it lists full applications exclusively
Components, Lightning data sets, and consultants available to hire
questions.explain: The lesson lists components that extend a screen, ready-to-use external data sets, and consultants as additional listing types.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how did Salesforce build out several of its "clouds," such as Marketing and Commerce?
options: By exclusively building every product line from scratch in-house
By purchasing Microsoft Dynamics 365 outright
By renaming its original CRM product multiple times
Partly through major acquisitions, such as ExactTarget and Demandware
questions.explain: The lesson names ExactTarget (marketing), Demandware (commerce), Tableau (analytics), and Slack (collaboration) as acquisitions that grew Salesforce's product lines.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect the platform/application distinction to Salesforce careers?
options: Administrators and developers do exactly the same work with no distinction
Only developers are allowed to use the Salesforce Platform at all
An administrator mostly configures existing applications, while a developer builds new custom applications directly on the platform
Administrators build new applications and developers only configure existing ones
questions.explain: The lesson previews Lesson 10's role breakdown: admins mostly customize pre-built applications, while developers build new things on the platform underneath.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a Salesforce "cloud" actually is?
options: A completely separate piece of software running on different infrastructure
A packaged product line built on the same underlying Salesforce Platform, not separate software
A storage location for uploaded files only
A term with no real technical meaning
questions.explain: Clouds like Sales Cloud and Service Cloud are product-line bundles of objects, features, and licenses, all built on one shared platform.

questions.q: What do sharing rules and org-wide defaults primarily control?
options: Which specific records a user can see, separate from their functional access
Which Salesforce edition the org is on
The order releases are rolled out in
Whether Multi-Factor Authentication is required
questions.explain: Sharing rules and org-wide defaults control record-level visibility — which specific rows a user can see — distinct from the functional access granted by profiles and permission sets.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an edition and a license?
options: Edition and license are two names for the exact same thing
Edition determines what features can exist in the org overall; license determines what a specific user can access
License determines the org's storage limit; edition determines nothing
Edition applies per user, while license applies to the whole org
questions.explain: Edition is an org-wide setting determining which features are even available, while licenses are assigned per user to control what each individual person can do.

questions.q: What does a Salesforce change set actually move between a Sandbox and Production?
options: All of the org's business records, like Accounts and Contacts
Metadata — the structural blueprint, such as fields, page layouts, and Flows
Only user login credentials
A full copy of the org's storage limits
questions.explain: Change sets deploy metadata — the configuration and structure — not the actual business data sitting in the source environment.

questions.q: What are the names of Salesforce's three annual releases, in order?
options: Spring, Summer, Winter
Winter, Spring, Fall
Alpha, Beta, General Availability
questions.explain: Salesforce ships three major releases a year named for their launch season: Spring (around February), Summer (around June), and Winter (around October, numbered for the following year).

questions.q: Why can Salesforce push a platform upgrade to every customer at the same time, three times a year?
options: Because every customer manually downloads and installs the update themselves
Because Salesforce only has a small number of customers to update
Because every customer runs the same application code on shared infrastructure, so one upgrade applies to everyone at once
Because upgrades are optional and most customers skip them
questions.explain: Since all tenants share the same underlying application, a single platform-wide upgrade reaches every customer simultaneously — nobody schedules a separate install.

questions.q: What is the difference between a profile and a permission set?
options: A permission set is a type of report; a profile is a type of dashboard
They are exactly the same thing with two different names
A profile is every user's one baseline access record; a permission set is an additional, stackable grant layered on top
A profile only applies to Sandboxes, never to Production
questions.explain: Every user has exactly one profile, which sets baseline access. Permission sets are additional, stackable grants layered on top without needing to change the profile.

questions.q: Why does the Sales app's Home page look completely different from the Customer Service app's Home page?
options: Each app's Home page is configured separately by an admin to surface relevant content for that job function
Home pages are randomly generated each time a user logs in
Only one app in an org is allowed to have a Home tab
The Home page always looks identical across every app
questions.explain: Home pages are built per app using the Lightning App Builder, so an admin can surface completely different components depending on the job function the app serves.

questions.q: What is a Salesforce 'app'?
options: A separately installed program outside the Salesforce platform
A curated, named bundle of tabs, logo, and color built for a specific job function
A type of custom object
The mobile version of Salesforce only
questions.explain: In Salesforce, an app is a lightweight concept: a named, curated set of tabs plus branding, tailored to a job function like Sales or Service — not a separately installed program.

questions.q: Why would a business create a custom object instead of using a standard one?
options: Because custom objects are required before any standard object can be used
Because their data doesn't fit any of the pre-built standard objects, like a university needing to track Courses
Because custom objects are faster to query than standard objects
Because standard objects can only hold ten records at a time
questions.explain: Custom objects exist for business data that doesn't map to any standard object — once created, they behave exactly like standard objects, complete with their own fields, records, and tab.

questions.q: In the mid-size company example, what happens when a customer who clicks a marketing email eventually becomes a sales deal?
options: They become a Lead, which Sales works into an Account, Contact, and Opportunity
They are automatically converted into a Case
Nothing changes in Salesforce until the deal closes
A new Salesforce org is created just for that customer
questions.explain: A marketing click typically creates a Lead, which Sales then works and converts into an Account, Contact, and Opportunity as the deal progresses.
